Session 44. ONE ticket: P2-112, the ATM breakeven monitor that silently never runs when there is no WPF dispatcher.

The four acceptance assertions were written BY HAND FIRST and are RED at the 1705/4 baseline. They live in tests/RiskGuardAddOnTests.cs, which you may NOT edit.

The entire change is ONE region in ONE file: addons/DynamicAtmManager.cs. Resist widening it. In particular do NOT touch MonitorTickCore, RequestStopMove, ModifyStopPrice or ReconcileStopFromBroker -- those were fixed by P0-67, are covered by ten tests, and are not what is wrong here.

READ THE TESTS BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING. They pin the seam's NAME (TryMarshal), its TYPE (Func<Action, bool>), and the log event type (ATM_MONITOR_NO_DISPATCHER). Getting any of the three wrong fails the ticket even if the logic is right.

tickets.title: P2-112: MonitorTick fails open with no dispatcher -- the ATM breakeven loop silently never runs
tickets.context:
THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG AND THERE IS A TEST THAT CATCHES IT. `P1-13`'s remedy was `RunGuardWork(label, work) => work()` -- run the work inline, always, and delete the dispatcher entirely. That justification does not transfer here. `MonitorTickCore` reaches `Account.Change()` through RequestStopMove -> ModifyStopPrice, and NT8 Account/Order/Position objects are not thread-safe, so running inline UNCONDITIONALLY would put a broker call on a Timer thread on every box that has a UI -- which is every box in normal use. `TestP2_112_WhenThereIsADispatcherTheSweepIsNotAlsoRunInline` asserts the sweep is NOT run inline when TryMarshal returns true, and it exists precisely to reject that shortcut. Keep the dispatcher path exactly as it is today when one is available; change only what happens when there is not.

WHY NOT MARSHAL JUST THE Account.Change() CALL: because there is nothing to marshal to. `Application.Current == null` means there is no WPF application object and therefore no UI thread anywhere in the process. Marshalling the broker call alone is only meaningful when a dispatcher exists, and when one exists this code already marshals the whole sweep, which is strictly safer. The fallback is unavoidably on the timer thread, and that is why it is announced rather than done quietly.

WHY THE `#if` MUST SHRINK RATHER THAN MOVE: the tests reach the real private `MonitorTick` by reflection and drive both branches through TryMarshal. They do this deliberately instead of using a new `#if TESTING` hook, because a hook is a second entry point that production never takes -- which is the exact arrangement that hid this defect for the life of the file. If any part of the branch logic stays behind `#if TESTING`, the tests are driving a body that does not ship and the ticket has not been done.

REACHABILITY, so you do not over-engineer: this box runs the NT8 GUI, so `Application.Current` is normally non-null and the defect is latent rather than active. It is banded `P2` on that basis. The fix is worth making because the failure mode is total and silent, not because it is firing today. Do not add retries, timers, or health surfaces for it.
